findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty data instead of the actual query results
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the new `<TableWidgetVisualization>` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` — these are hardcoded literals, not derived from `result`/`tableResults` (the actual query results used by the `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch). As a result, any dashboard/table widget rendered with this flag enabled will always show an empty table regardless of the underlying data, while the legacy branch (flag disabled) continues to show real data. This looks like an unfinished wiring of the new table visualization component into the widget card. There is also no test exercising this new conditional branch in chart.tsx.

findings.title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references the wrong class for _truncate_title
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is a `@staticmethod` defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, and it calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`. However `_truncate_title` is defined as a staticmethod on `CommitContextIntegration` itself, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` (subclasses of `PRCommentWorkflow`) call `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` in `get_comment_body`. Unless `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit from `CommitContextIntegration` (which is not indicated by the sibling `OpenPRCommentWorkflow(ABC)` pattern that takes `integration: CommitContextIntegration` as a composed attribute rather than a base class), this call will raise `AttributeError: type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title'` at runtime, breaking the merged-PR suspect-issue comment feature for both GitHub and GitLab integrations.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with get_multi results purely by positional zip
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` to reconstruct each `ErrorEvent`. This assumes the dict returned by `get_multi` preserves the same ordering as the input `node_ids`/`error_ids` list. If the backend returns results in a different order (e.g. due to internal batching, concurrent fetches, or sorting), this will silently associate the wrong title/message/timestamp with an error id, corrupting the generated AI summary input. A keyed lookup (`events.get(node_id)`) would be safer than relying on dict insertion order matching input order.

findings.title: Likely timestamp unit mismatch when interleaving error events with breadcrumb events
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves `error_events` (whose `timestamp` comes from the stored event's `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`, which is Unix epoch seconds) with breadcrumb/recording events read from segment data, comparing `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Recording/rrweb events conventionally carry `timestamp` in milliseconds since epoch, not seconds. If that holds here, comparing a seconds-based error timestamp against millisecond-based event timestamps will produce badly out-of-order interleaving (errors will appear to occur either far before or far after all breadcrumbs). The accompanying test (`test_get_with_error`) constructs both the breadcrumb and error timestamps from the same `now.timestamp()` (seconds) value, which masks this potential unit mismatch rather than verifying correct behavior against realistic millisecond-based breadcrumb timestamps.

findings.title: Environment filter silently dropped when fetching trace item attribute keys
findings.body: `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` builds the query options for the trace-items attributes endpoint but no longer includes `environment`, with a comment stating it's "left out intentionally as it's not supported". The previous implementation in `useTraceItemAttributeKeys` sent `environment: selection.environments` to the same endpoint. If the endpoint does use this parameter, consumers of the new shared hook (`useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys`/`useTraceItemAttributeKeys`) will now fetch attribute keys across all environments instead of the selected one, silently changing results for any caller that previously relied on environment scoping.

findings.title: Undocumented default-behavior change for autofix automation tuning, unrelated to stated PR scope
findings.body: `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` default is changed from `"low"` to `"off"` (mirrored in `src/sentry/constants.py`'s `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT`). This silently changes behavior for every project that has not explicitly set this option, turning off automatic Seer autofix runs on new issues by default. The PR description ("Test 5") gives no rationale for this change, and it is unrelated to the stated "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System" scope, making it hard for reviewers to assess whether this regression/intentional change is safe to ship alongside the rest of the PR.
